extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in NRC adjudicatory proceedings; presiding officers; NRC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing prehearing conferences, scheduling, discovery, evidence, settlement, and decisionmaking in NRC adjudicatory proceedings under 10 CFR Part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference order requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall enter an order that recites the action taken at the conference, the amendments allowed to the pleadings and agreements by the parties, and the issues or matters in controversy to be determined in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any objections to the order must be filed within five (5) days after service; parties may not file replies unless directed; filing objections does not stay the decision unless ordered; presiding officer may revise the order in light of objections and may certify matters under §2.319(l); the order controls the subsequent course of the proceeding unless modified for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may stipulate in writing at any stage or orally during the hearing any relevant fact or the contents/authenticity of any document; parties may also stipulate to procedure to be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulations may be received in evidence. Upon motion of all parties, presiding officer may recognize stipulations to govern conduct of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument before the presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer may allow and fix time for presentation of oral argument when time permits and the nature of the proceeding and public interest warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer will impose appropriate time limits. The transcript of the argument is part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer shall enter a scheduling order establishing limits for time to file motions, conclude discovery, commence oral phase (if applicable), and take other actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling order may include modifications of disclosure times under §§2.336 and 2.704, dates for prehearing conferences, and other matters appropriate to the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of model milestones in scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing the scheduling order, the presiding officer shall utilize the applicable model milestones in Appendix B as a starting point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer must modify milestones based on number of contentions admitted, issue complexity, party considerations, NRC staff schedule for safety/environmental evaluations, and NRC interest in fair and expeditious resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of scheduling order
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling order must aim to achieve proper case management purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include: expediting disposition; establishing early/continuous control to avoid protraction; discouraging wasteful prehearing activities; improving hearing quality through preparation; and facilitating settlement (including ADR) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of NRC staff schedule in scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer must consider NRC staff's projected schedule for safety and environmental evaluations to avoid adverse impacts on staff's ability to complete reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearings on safety issues may start before NRC safety evaluation if it would expedite the proceeding; EIS-related environmental hearings may not commence before issuance of final EIS; discovery against NRC staff on safety/environmental issues should be suspended until SER or EIS is issued unless presiding officer finds early discovery won't adversely affect completion and will expedite hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to limit cumulative witnesses and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent unnecessary delays or an unnecessarily large record, the presiding officer may limit witnesses whose testimony would be cumulative and may strike certain evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May strike argumentative, repetitious, cumulative, unreliable, immaterial, or irrelevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination plan filing and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party or participant requesting permission to conduct cross-examination must file a cross-examination plan for each witness or panel proposed to be cross-examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer shall require conformance to the filed plan and may take measures to prevent argumentative, repetitious, or cumulative cross-examination; may impose time limits on arguments considering evidence volume and issue complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain and modify hearing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer shall take appropriate action to maintain the hearing schedule for completion of the evidentiary record and issuance of initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing schedule may be modified only for good cause; in making good cause determination consider diligence, unavoidable circumstances, party agreement and overall effect. Presiding officer must notify Commission in writing if delays exceed specified thresholds (more than 45 days for major activities or 60 days for record/initial decision), including reasons and mitigation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on attacking Commission rules in adjudication; waiver/exception petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, Commission licensing rules are not subject to attack in adjudicatory proceedings, but a participant may petition for waiver or exception on the sole ground that special circumstances make application of the rule not serve its purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include an affidavit identifying specific aspects and particularity of special circumstances; other participants may respond by counter-affidavit; presiding officer evaluates prima facie showing and may preclude evidence if prima facie not made; if prima facie shown, presiding officer must certify matter to Commission for determination; participants may alternatively file a petition for rulemaking under §2.802.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures by parties (general discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise ordered, all parties other than NRC staff must, within 30 days of order granting hearing or petition to intervene, disclose names/contacts of persons (including experts) they rely on and provide copies/description of all documents and data compilations relevant to their contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only description provided, other parties have right to request copies. When documents are publicly available, sufficient disclosure is location, title and page reference. Parties must also list documents claimed privileged with sufficient information to assess privilege claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff initial disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: NRC staff must, within 30 days of order granting hearing or petition to intervene, disclose to the extent available (excluding privileged): application/requests relevant to contentions; NRC correspondence with applicant relevant; documents supporting or opposing the application that support staff's review and are relevant; staff documents representing staff's determination that are relevant; and list privileged documents with information to assess claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 30-day timing and exclusions for privileged materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to update disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must update their disclosures every month after initial disclosures on a due date selected by the presiding officer (unless parties agree otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates limited to documents subject to disclosure and need not include documents developed/obtained/discovered during two weeks before due date; updates must include previously undisclosed documents; duty to update ends when presiding officer resolves the contention or as otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for failure to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer may impose sanctions for continuing unexcused failure to make required disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include dismissal of specific contentions, dismissal of adjudication, denial/dismissal of application or use of discovery provisions in subpart G; may prohibit admission into evidence of documents or testimony of undisclosed witnesses unless party demonstrates good cause for failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards Information access criteria and dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: If dispute over disclosure of Safeguards Information arises, presiding officer may order disclosure only if the individual seeking access has requisite 'need to know', has undergone FBI criminal history check (subject to certain exemptions and procedural protections), and Office of Administration found the individual trustworthy and reliable (subject to review procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Administration must provide records considered, allow challenges within 10 days, resolve challenges; individuals may request review of adverse determinations by Chief Administrative Judge who designates another officer to review; timelines: request for review filed within 15 days, staff response within 10 days, designated officer decision within 15 days; reversal only upon finding abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective terms and safeguarding of Safeguards Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer may include protective terms and conditions (including affidavits of nondisclosure) to prevent unauthorized disclosure of Safeguards Information and may prescribe additional procedures to safeguard info with minimum impairment of procedural rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards Information must also be protected per §§73.21 and 73.22/73.23; violations of protection provisions may be subject to civil penalty under §2.205 and criminal penalties under Section 223 (considered issued under Section 161b); if no presiding officer yet appointed, authority resides in officer with jurisdiction under §2.318(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible discovery under §2.336
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosures required by §2.336 constitute the sole discovery permitted for NRC proceedings under this part unless further discovery is provided under the specific subpart or Commission orders otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits discovery absent specific provision otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Only relevant, material, and reliable evidence which is not unduly repetitious will be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immaterial or irrelevant parts of an admissible document will be segregated and excluded so far as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection content and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection to evidence must briefly state the grounds of objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcript must include the objection, the grounds, and the ruling. Exception to an adverse ruling is preserved without notation on-the-record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An offer of proof made in connection with an objection to exclusion of oral testimony must state the substance of the proffered evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If excluded evidence is written, a copy must be marked for identification. Rejected exhibits, adequately marked, must be retained in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits marking and e-filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits must be marked in accordance with presiding officer instructions and filed through the agency's E-Filing system unless exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exhibit is not filed through E-Filing, a duplicate is admissible to same extent as original unless authenticity is questioned or admission would be unfair. Information referenced via hyperlinks must be submitted in entirety either as part of the exhibit or as a separate exhibit to be included in the evidentiary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An official record of a government agency may be evidenced by an official publication or by a copy attested by the officer having legal custody and accompanied by a certificate of their custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for authenticating official records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice procedure and opportunities to controvert
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission or presiding officer may take official notice of facts judicially noticeable by U.S. courts or technical/scientific facts within Commission knowledge as an expert body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each noticed fact must be specified in the record with sufficient particularity to advise parties and each adversely affected party must be given opportunity to controvert. If decision rests in whole/part on official notice not previously subject to opportunity to controvert, a party may controvert by filing an appeal from an initial decision or petition for reconsideration, clearly setting forth information relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff evidence obligations in application proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings involving construction permits, operating licenses, or other applications, the NRC staff must offer into evidence certain staff reports, safety evaluations, EISs, and may provide sponsoring witnesses depending on whether the NRC staff is a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics vary by context: e.g., ACRS reports and safety evaluations are to be offered in construction-permit proceedings; in other applications staff shall offer ACRS reports and, at discretion, safety evaluations/testimony, §2.1202(a) statement of position, and EIS/EA if there are admitted contentions regarding adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and availability of settlement and ADR
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair and reasonable settlement and resolution of issues is encouraged; parties have the opportunity to submit proposed settlements or request alternative dispute resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer may, upon joint motion, request Chief Administrative Judge to appoint a Settlement Judge to conduct negotiations or remit to ADR. Settlement Judge may convene conferences, report status, and may not discuss merits with Chief Administrative Judge or appear as witness. Settlement negotiations terminate upon order of Chief Administrative Judge; decisions about appointing or terminating Settlement Judge not subject to review by presiding officer or Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of attorneys/representatives and settlement authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer or Settlement Judge may require that the attorney expected to try the case and parties or agents with full settlement authority be present or available during settlement negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence may be required in-person or by telephone to facilitate negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of settlement negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: No evidence, statements, or conduct in settlement negotiations will be admissible in any subsequent hearing, except by stipulation of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents disclosed during negotiations may not be used in litigation unless obtained through appropriate discovery or subpoena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of additional requirements for settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer or Settlement Judge may impose additional requirements on parties and interested persons as necessary for fair and efficient resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary measures to ensure efficient settlement process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of settlement negotiations on jurisdiction and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement negotiations do not divest the presiding officer of jurisdiction and do not automatically stay the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hearing must not be unduly delayed because of settlement negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and required content of settlement agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement must be in the form of a proposed settlement agreement, a consent order, and a motion for its entry that includes reasons why it should be accepted and must be signed by consenting parties or authorized representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed settlement must contain: (1) admission of all jurisdictional facts; (2) express waiver of further procedural steps and rights to challenge or seek judicial review; (3) statement that order has same force and effect as an order after full hearing; and (4) statement that matters required to be adjudicated have been resolved by the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and finalization of settlement agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following issuance of a notice of hearing, a settlement must be approved by the presiding officer or the Commission to be binding in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer or Commission may order adjudication of issues required in public interest; in enforcement proceedings presiding officer shall accord due weight to NRC staff position; if approved, terms must be embodied in a decision or order. Settlements approved by presiding officer are subject to Commission review under §2.341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited decisionmaking procedure criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer may determine a proceeding by order after hearing without issuing an initial decision when certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) all parties stipulate that initial decision may be omitted and waive rights to petition for review, request oral argument, and seek judicial review; (2) no unresolved substantial issue of fact, law, or discretion remains and record clearly warrants relief requested; (3) presiding officer finds dispensing with initial decision is in the public interest. Orders under this paragraph are subject to Commission review on its own motion within 40 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness of initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial decision may be made effective immediately, subject to Commission review within 30 days, when parties stipulate and waive rights and no unresolved substantial issue remains and presiding officer finds immediate effectiveness in public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain authorizations/permits/licenses are excluded from this provision (listed statutory/part exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision findings in operating-license contested proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In any initial decision in a contested proceeding on an application for an operating license or renewed license, the presiding officer shall make findings of fact and conclusions of law on matters put into controversy by the parties and any matter designated by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer also may consider matters not put in controversy by the parties if designated by the Commission to be decided by the presiding officer.
